# Ectolens's copy of KQuickImageEditor

KQuickImageEditor 0.7.0 (KDE, <https://invent.kde.org/libraries/kquickimageeditor>, LGPL-2.1-or-later, its own files under `LICENSES/`), taken into Ectolens on 2026-11-02 so the Text and Number marks can have Ectolens's look. The marks are drawn inside this library, so their look can't change from Ectolens's side. Upstream's README.md is next to this file.

Ectolens builds it into the `ectolens` binary: a static library (`EctolensImageEditor`) and a static QML module under its own name, `org.kde.kquickimageeditor.ectolens`, imported in `src/Main.cpp` (`Q_IMPORT_QML_PLUGIN`). Plasma's installed KQuickImageEditor is never loaded next to it. Its settings are the same keys as upstream's, in the `[Annotations]` group of `ectolensrc`, so choices made before carry over.

## What differs from 0.7.0, and why

- **The Text and Number look**: a nicer default look for both, in Ecto green.
  - `src/annotations/traits.h`, `traits.cpp`: a Text mark with a visible fill is a label, its words on a rounded box padded around them (`fillPath`, `textLabelPadding`, `textLabelRadius`); a Number wider than its circle becomes a pill (`createTextPath`). Labels and badges carry a hairline ring one shade darker than the fill, and their words take near-black or white, whichever reads on the fill (`isLabel`, `labelRingColor`, `labelTextColor`). The label's box counts for its drawn area and its clicks (`createVisualRect`, `createInteractivePath`).
  - `src/annotations/annotationdocument.cpp`: paints the label box, the ring and the words' color; a text mark's fill turning on or off rebuilds its box (`SelectedItemWrapper::setFillColor`).
  - `src/annotations/utils.h`: the shadow follows the label's box; `textLabelPadding` and `labelTextColor` for QML.
  - `src/annotations/annotationtool.cpp`: the Text tool has a fill (its label), saved as `textFillColor`.
  - `src/annotationconfig.kcfg`: Text and Number start Ecto green (#c8f22e) in Geist Semibold (11 pt and 10 pt); `textFillColor` is new.
  - `src/annotations/TextTool.qml`: the editing box lines up with a label (it follows the words, its outline goes around the box, the move handle clears it) and its cursor takes the words' color.
- **Text boxes**: a drag with the Text tool draws a box whose words wrap inside it.
  - `src/annotations/traits.h`, `traits.cpp`: `Text::box`, the outside size of a box drawn for a Text mark (a label's box). Its words wrap inside it, at word boundaries or, for a word too long for a line, anywhere; it keeps its drawn size and grows down only so no words are hidden, and its words never get narrower than two line heights, so a much bigger font widens the box rather than stacking letters (`createTextPath`, `textBoxWordsSize`, `textBoxLines`, `drawTextWords`, `textBoxMinimumSize`, `textBoxDragThreshold`, `textBoxWordsTopLeft`, `textOutsideRect`). A Text mark's words, a box's and a label's alike, are laid out in a `QTextDocument` set up as Qt Quick's `TextEdit` sets up its own (`wordsDocument`, after `QQuickTextEditPrivate::updateDefaultTextOption`: the alignment, swapped left for right only for words with a right-to-left letter, the words' direction from their first strong letter as `QQuickTextEdit::q_textChanged` finds it, or the input method's, the font at Qt Quick's 0.5 pt, `wordsFont`, which a label is measured in too), so the editing box's cursor sits on the painted words in any language; upstream painted with `QPainter::drawText`, left to right ("TODO: RTL language reversal"), and replaced tabs with spaces in anything but left-aligned text. A Number is painted with `drawText` as before. All of a box takes clicks, label or not (`createInteractivePath`).
  - Alignment (`Text::alignment`, `horizontal`, `vertical`): words sit left, centered or right on the picture whatever their language (the editing box's explicit `horizontalAlignment`, which swaps left and right for right-to-left words so that its layout's own swap puts them back), and, in a box taller than its words, at its top, middle or bottom (offset as `QQuickTextUtil::alignedY` offsets the editing box's, `textWordsTopOffset`). A label sized to its words grows from its aligned side as words are added and when its font changes, and a new one starts with that side at the click (`keepTextAnchor`), as tldraw's text does (`TextShapeUtil.onBeforeUpdate`). `textCursorPoints` gives where the cursor stands before each character, for the tests. Each block of the document is drawn once at the words' top left (a block's layout holds its own place in the document; adding it again painted a box's second paragraph a line too low).
  - `src/annotations/annotationdocument.cpp`, `annotationdocument.h`, `annotationdocument_p.h`: a drag with the Text tool draws a box from where it began (upstream moved the new text with the pointer) (`beginItem` keeps `creationPressPoint`, `continueItem`). `SelectedItemWrapper` gains `textBox`, `textOutsideRect`, `textBoxSize` (the size drawn, before growing for words) and `setTextBox`. A font change keeps a box where it was drawn, its words moving inside as the padding follows the font (`setFont`). Box words are painted by `Traits::drawTextWords`. While a box is drawn, Shift makes it square and Ctrl draws it out from the press as its center, as for the rectangle (`continueItem`). `SelectedItemWrapper::textAlignment` reads and sets a mark's alignment (a label with no words yet moves so the point it was started at is its new aligned side); a new Text mark takes the Text tool's (`beginItem`). Words typed and not yet saved (TextTool.qml saves them a moment after the last key) are saved before the mark is let go, another is taken or made, and before an undo or redo (`SelectedItemWrapperPrivate::savePendingWords`, called from `beginItem`, `selectItem`, `deselectItem`, `undo`, `redo`, `cropCanvas`, `applyTransform` and `applyColorAdjustment`, so the words keep their place before a crop, turn or color change); upstream lost the words typed in the last quarter second before a click elsewhere. `SelectedItemWrapper::commitTyping` saves words, taking the place of the mark's first save of its words when that is the latest step (`SelectedItemWrapperPrivate::firstWordsSave`, set by `commitChanges` when it saves a new mark).
  - `src/annotations/annotationtool.h`, `annotationtool.cpp`, `src/annotationconfig.kcfg`: the Text tool's alignment, `textAlignment` (one across and one up and down, saved as `textAlignment`, Left and Top to start; anything else is refused).
  - `src/annotations/annotationviewport.cpp`: with the Text tool, a pointer that stays within 8 of the window's logical pixels of the press (whatever the zoom; 14 physical pixels at 1.75 scale) is a click, today's label; once it goes farther it draws a box.
  - `src/annotations/utils.h`: the shadow paints a box's words wrapped; `textBoxMinimumSize`, `textLabelRadius`, `labelRingColor` and `textTabStopDistance` for QML.
  - `src/annotations/TextTool.qml`: the editing box wraps for a box (`wrapMode: TextEdit.Wrap`, with its width set, since Qt Quick's TextEdit wraps only at a set width), takes the label's padding for a box with or without a label, shows the label while a drawn box has no words yet, takes presses in a box's or a label's padding (`containmentMask`, `outsideArea`) so they place the cursor instead of starting a new mark (upstream started one from a label's padding), sets its alignment from the mark's (`horizontalAlignment`, and `verticalAlignment` in a box), and gives a box handles on its edges and corners that resize it (the words rewrap). Only boxes get handles; a plain label is as before. Each handle takes the pointer on its part outside the box and a 2-pixel band along the edge, so none covers the words, through a `MouseArea` that also resizes on the release (a `DragHandler` dropped a drag whose motion reached Qt only with the release); a side handle keeps the height the box was drawn to, so it shrinks back as words go. The move handle stands clear of a box's handles at any zoom, beside right-aligned words on the right and other words on the left, placed by `x` (anchoring one side after the other, as the alignment changes, left it as wide as both made it). Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z go to the picture's history while a mark is written (`Keys.onShortcutOverride`, `Keys.onPressed`): the editing box claims them for its own undo whenever it can be typed in (`QQuickTextControl`'s common text shortcuts), so upstream's Ctrl+Z took typing back even after a handle drag, a move or a choice in the options rail, and its own undo could not stay in step with the picture's. A mark's first letter is saved at once, as upstream (so a new mark is painted, exported and kept at once: the picture paints a mark from its saved step), and the next save of its words takes that step's place (`commitTyping`), so words typed in one go are one step to undo, not a first letter left behind; words not yet saved are saved as their own step before a handle drag, a move, a choice in the options rail or the Shadow button. The editing box's right-click Undo and Redo are the picture's too (`private/TextContextMenu.qml`, its `document`). The text Binding's value follows the editing box's own words while nothing is shown: taken again before the editing box finished hiding, a mark got the last one's empty words written into it (upstream, wiping its words).
- **The editing box's tab width** (an upstream bug, fixed here): `TextTool.qml` set `tabStopDistance: Math.round(fontMetrics.advanceWidth("x") * 8)`, which QML doesn't reevaluate when the font changes, so the cursor kept the first font's tab width and wandered off words after a tab. It is now `Utils.textTabStopDistance(font)`. Found by `annotation_look_test`; `textToolBreaksLikePainting` loads the real TextTool.qml and holds its lines to the painted ones after a font change, which upstream's binding fails.
- **`AnnotationDocument::clearRedo()`** (for undo and redo of the overlay's frame too): forgets the steps that could be redone, as a new step does, so a change to the frame after an undo drops the marks' redo steps. Ectolens's `FrameHistory` calls it. `src/annotations/annotationdocument.{h,cpp}`.
- **The QML name.** Every `import org.kde.kquickimageeditor` in the QML files reads `import org.kde.kquickimageeditor.ectolens`.
- **No Highway.** `src/annotations/stackblur.cpp` is the stack blur in plain C++ (same interface, same formats, same kernel) instead of upstream's Highway (SIMD) version, whose headers aren't installed here. `autotests/stackblurtest.cpp` adds a test holding it exactly to a direct, pixel-by-pixel average. `stackblur_opencv.cpp` and the Highway benchmark are left out.
- **GCC 13** (found 2026-11-05 by the install's stranger check on KDE neon, which is built on Ubuntu 24.04): `src/annotations/coloradjustment.cpp`'s `IsIdentity` concept tests the matrix flags with plain bit arithmetic, `(MF & MF_General) == 0`, where upstream (0.7.0 and master as of 2026-11-05) builds a constexpr `MatrixFlags` and calls `testAnyFlags`, which GCC 13 rejects ("used before its definition"). Same meaning; GCC 14 and newer took either.
- **The build.** `CMakeLists.txt` (here, replacing upstream's top-level and `src/` ones), `autotests/CMakeLists.txt`, `src/kquickimageeditor_export.h` (nothing to export from a static library) and `include/KQuickImageEditor/` (the forwarding headers upstream generates). The shaders are compiled with Qt's `qsb` tool directly, so Qt ShaderTools' CMake package isn't needed. Upstream's docs (`*.qdoc`, `*.qdocconf`) are left out.

Not taken from the release at all: its top-level CMake files (`CMakeLists.txt`, `CMakePresets.json`, `KQuickImageEditorConfig.cmake.in`), `examples/`, `tests/`, `koko-animation.mp4`, and its CI and editor files. Everything else is 0.7.0 as released.

## Taking a newer release

Unpack the release somewhere else and compare it with the 0.7.0 release (`diff -ru`) to see what KDE changed; carry those changes into the files here by hand rather than copying folders over, since copying would bring back what is left out (`src/CMakeLists.txt`, `stackblur_opencv.cpp`, the docs, the Highway benchmark) and overwrite the changes above. Then run `ctest --test-dir build/spectacle -R "stackblur|annotation_look"` and the `annotate`, `textbox` and `window` off-screen runs (`tests/e2e/overlay`).
